data.title: Test Data and Fixture
data.tagline: Test data are input and state samples; a fixture is a reusable setup and cleanup mechanism.
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish data values from a reusable mechanism that prepares and resets those values for tests.
data.description: A fixed user and order JSON are test data. Creating an account and order before a test, then deleting or restoring state afterward, is a fixture. Together they give each case the same start. One random input or yesterday’s leftover record is not stable evidence.

learning.assumes: You know a second test run should not be changed by data left from the first.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish data values from a reusable mechanism that prepares and resets those values for tests.

distinctions.label: Test double
distinctions.explanation: A Test Data and Fixture gives tests a repeatable starting point and cleans up afterward. A Test Double replaces the behavior of a real dependency.

explanation.title: Test data supplies clear input and state
explanation.text: A registered user, cart with two items, and valid coupon are starting conditions. Fixed readable data makes failures reviewable instead of randomly different every run.

explanation.title: A fixture restores the same starting point
explanation.text: Fixtures organize account creation, order setup, dependency startup, and cleanup into a reusable mechanism. Cases write less duplicated setup and do not contaminate each other with leftovers.

data.boundary: Test data and fixtures are related but distinct: data are values and state samples; fixtures prepare and clean up those prerequisites. One random input or a manually left database row cannot replace a repeatable fixture.

lessonPractice.title: Which test setup creates a regular user and a pending-payment order before each test, then removes them afterward?

options.label: A fixture, because it defines setup before and cleanup after a case
options.feedback: Correct. The user name and order amount are test data; the reusable setup and cleanup flow is the fixture.

options.label: Only test data, because it contains a user and order
options.feedback: It describes not only values but how state is created and restored around every run.

options.label: Production seed data that needs no cleanup
options.feedback: Test prerequisites should not pollute real production data and should restore a stable starting point.

data.agentPrompt: Create an order-test fixture: before each test make a fixed user and pending-payment order, then clean up afterward. Keep concrete test data separate from setup/cleanup steps; run twice and confirm the second run is not affected by the first.
